pharm: Broad-spectrum imidazole antifungal; inhibits fungal cytochrome P450 14-alpha-demethylase, reducing ergosterol synthesis and disrupting the fungal cell membrane. Available as topical, intravaginal, and oral troche formulations.

summary: Clotrimazole is a broad-spectrum imidazole antifungal used topically for dermatophyte infections (tinea pedis, cruris, corporis) and cutaneous candidiasis, intravaginally for vulvovaginal candidiasis, and as an oral troche for oropharyngeal candidiasis. Systemic absorption from topical and vaginal use is minimal, so it is generally well tolerated, with the oral troche being the only form requiring periodic liver-enzyme monitoring with prolonged use.
indications: Oropharyngeal candidiasis (oral troche, treatment and prophylaxis)

moa: Clotrimazole is an imidazole antifungal that inhibits fungal cytochrome P450 lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, blocking conversion of lanosterol to ergosterol. The resulting depletion of ergosterol and accumulation of toxic sterol precursors damages the fungal cell membrane and increases its permeability, producing fungistatic to fungicidal activity against dermatophytes and Candida species.

preg: Topical and intravaginal clotrimazole is generally considered acceptable in pregnancy because of minimal systemic absorption; intravaginal use is commonly recommended for vulvovaginal candidiasis (a 7-day regimen is often preferred). Use the oral troche only if clearly needed. Consult a clinician before use during pregnancy.
lact: Clotrimazole is considered compatible with breastfeeding; systemic absorption from topical and vaginal use is negligible. Avoid applying topical product directly to the breast/nipple area where the infant may ingest it, or wash before nursing.
renal: No dosage adjustment needed; systemic absorption from topical, vaginal, and oral troche use is minimal.
hepatic: No adjustment for topical/vaginal use. With the oral troche, mild elevations of AST have been reported; obtain periodic liver function tests during prolonged oral therapy.

moderate: Topical clotrimazole may reduce efficacy of and damage latex condoms/diaphragms (avoid concurrent latex contraceptive reliance during vaginal therapy)

missed: Topical/vaginal: apply the missed dose as soon as remembered; if near the next dose, skip it and resume the schedule - do not double-apply. Oral troche: take the missed troche when remembered and continue, but do not double the dose. Single-dose vaginal regimens: not applicable.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with topical or vaginal use given minimal systemic absorption. Accidental ingestion of topical/vaginal product or excessive troche use may cause nausea, vomiting, or GI upset; manage with supportive care. There is no specific antidote.
